title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a random experiment as one whose possible outcomes are known but whose result in a single trial cannot be predicted.
Explain probability as a measure of how likely an event is, distinguishing subjective judgement from objective estimates.
State that probability lies on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
Describe and rank events as impossible, less likely, even chance, more likely or certain.
Calculate experimental probability as the number of times an event occurred divided by the total number of trials.
Distinguish the frequency of an event from its relative frequency in observed data.
Decide whether the outcomes of an experiment are equally likely.
Calculate theoretical probability as favourable outcomes divided by possible outcomes.

topics.title: Statistical data, sampling and the long run

concepts.learning_objective: Estimate probabilities from sample data and use them to make predictions for a population.
Explain that experimental probability tends towards theoretical probability as the number of trials increases.
Recognise that independent trials have no memory, so past results do not change the next probability.
Write the sample space of an experiment, listing every outcome exactly once, and find its size n(S).
Identify an event as a subset of the sample space and list its outcomes.
Use a tree diagram to list all outcomes of a multi-step experiment.
Find probabilities of events in multi-step experiments using a tree diagram.
